Recursion is a programming technique where a function calls itself to solve a smaller version of the same problem. It works by defining a base case that stops the recursion and a recursive case that moves the problem toward that base case. Each recursive call adds a new layer to the call stack, and when the base case is reached, the stack unwinds, returning results back up. By breaking problems into similar subproblems, recursion can simplify tasks such as calculating factorials or traversing tree structures. 
--- END OF TRANSCRIPT ---
